quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: On a slippery road, you should keep a following distance that is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Farther than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road. Always increase your following distance when driving on wet or slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should move back into your lane when:

options.text: You can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You have passed the front bumper of the other vehicle.
You are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Move back into your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. This gives you enough safe space.

questions.question: Downward-facing triangular signs tell you to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to other traffic.
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs mean yield. Slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians pass before you continue.

questions.question: This sign warns that:

options.text: Trucks are not allowed on an upcoming hill.
Trucks are on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that a steep hill or downgrade is coming.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, turn into:
questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the first available legal lane. When turning onto a one-way street, this means the first lane in the direction you are turning.

questions.question: This sign means the road ahead:
questions.correctAnswerText: Curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a reverse curve. The road curves to the right first, then to the left.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You may turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You may turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic moves to the left. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: You may not park:

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane. When parking on the street, you must stay within 12 inches of the curb.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are on your left and parked cars are on your right. You should steer:
questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle, between both.
questions.explanation: When trapped between oncoming traffic and parked cars, steer down the middle. This gives you the best chance to avoid both.

questions.question: A steady green light means you:

options.text: Must slow down and be ready to stop.
Must stop and check for oncoming traffic.
May go through if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: May go through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection if it is safe. You may turn right or left unless a sign says otherwise. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are stopped behind other vehicles at a stop sign. After the vehicles ahead pass through and there is no cross traffic, you:

options.text: May go through the intersection without stopping again.
Must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going through.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the vehicle directly ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going through.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip this step just because other vehicles are ahead of you.

questions.question: It is best to keep space between your vehicle and other vehicles:

options.text: Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to dangers. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Low beams work better in fog than high beams because high beams reflect light back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: For drivers 21 years or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent or higher.
questions.explanation: Drivers 21 or older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided red sign means stop.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Know that tinted windows reduce visibility in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking at oncoming headlights causes your pupils to shrink. When the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the darkness. During this time, you cannot see clearly.

questions.question: If two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
The vehicle on the right must let the vehicle on the left go first.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should go without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must let the vehicle on the right go first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you may pass. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the road shoulder with no one inside.
When it approaches you, even if the lights are not flashing.
On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a two-lane road when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic from both directions must stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is out.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes:

options.text: Use the rearview mirror inside your car.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show everything. There are blind spots that you can only see by turning your head and looking over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: What driving technique helps you avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better traction.
Leave the highways as soon as possible.
Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow or ice. This is the best way to avoid crashes. Also increase the distance between you and the car ahead.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: The blind spots around trucks and buses.
A road where stereo volume is restricted.
A TV show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The blind spots around trucks and buses.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, the back, and the front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These areas are called the "No zone."

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea in bad weather.
Okay if you don't know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because other drivers may get frustrated and try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous. Drivers behind you may become impatient and take risky chances to pass you.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines in the middle of the road mean?

options.text: You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either side. You may only cross these lines to turn left or pass pedestrians, cyclists, or scooter/skateboard riders when it is safe.

questions.question: You see a flashing red traffic light ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down and drive carefully through.
Stop completely, look both ways, and go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, look both ways, and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, let other traffic and pedestrians pass, and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol content (BAC) and its effects on your body.
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol and its effects from your body.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not permitted?

options.text: On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill. You may not see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on the left, and a cyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Let the car pass, then pass the cyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the cyclist.
questions.explanation: When there are multiple hazards, handle them one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then pass the cyclist when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do at a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
You don't need to stop if the intersection looks clear.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield before entering the intersection.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat it like a four-way stop sign. Stop completely and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic signal ahead shows red.
The traffic signal ahead shows green.
There is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic light is coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: You see heavy smoke ahead on the road. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move to the right as far as possible, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beams and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right as far as possible, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: When you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down right away. Move as far right as you can and stop off the road. Then check if it is safe to continue. Some smoke can hurt your eyes, lungs, or be deadly.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Use cruise control near railroad crossings to keep a steady speed.
You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
You have the right-of-way at railroad crossings and do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal tells you to. Drive carefully near railroad tracks.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded road areas under trees or buildings. These areas freeze faster than other parts of the road and are the last to dry.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: You can eliminate them by having one outside mirror on each side.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
You can check blind spots by looking in your rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most cars.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Large trucks have much larger blind spots. Other drivers should avoid these areas.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road may be slippery when wet. Drive carefully on slippery roads.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, so you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Drive at a safe speed for the conditions to avoid needing hard braking.

questions.question: A driver turning left must yield to a bicyclist coming from the opposite direction.
questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles just as you would to oncoming cars. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn. Turn only when it is clear of all traffic and people.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what ensures safe driving?

options.text: Get a ride home with a sober friend.
Take a cold shower before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with a sober friend.
questions.explanation: The best way to avoid drunk driving is to have a sober friend drive you home. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your blood. Your body needs about one hour to remove the alcohol from one drink.

questions.question: A red painted curb means:

options.text: The area is for picking up or dropping off passengers only.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking, standing, or stopping.
questions.explanation: You cannot stop, stand, or park at a red curb.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Follow closely in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Stay farther back than you would behind a car.
Stay one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than you would behind a car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, you block the driver's view in the side mirrors. The truck driver cannot see you. Tailgating any vehicle is dangerous because you lose your safety cushion if they stop suddenly.

questions.question: At a yield sign, what should you do?

options.text: Yield only to traffic on the right.
Yield only to traffic on the left.
Slow down and let other traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let other traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let traffic in the intersection or on the road you are entering go first.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead. These might include a change in traffic direction, a steep downgrade, or a hazard that needs your attention.

questions.question: What does a green arrow with a red light mean?

options.text: You may only drive in the direction of the arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to go any direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may only drive in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction of the arrow. Make sure the intersection is clear before you go.

questions.question: How do you see vehicles in your blind spots?
questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. To check them, you must look over your shoulders.

questions.question: When should you use high beam headlights?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use high beams whenever there are no nearby vehicles. High beams help you see twice as far as low beams. Use them on unfamiliar roads, in construction areas, or where people may be walking along the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Circular signs indicate railroad crossings. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead. Watch for signs of an approaching train.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow centerlines mean that traffic from both directions cannot cross the center to pass.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and traffic is backing up behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off to the right and let traffic pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off to the right and let traffic pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic is dangerous. On a two-lane road, if traffic is backing up behind you, pull off the road to let other vehicles pass. Only drive below the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: Motorcycles are entitled to:

options.text: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the full lane width, just like all other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign means it is not safe to enter the road or driveway from your current direction. If you see this sign, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No one can pass.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. They mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: A bus is signaling to return to the roadway after stopping. What must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to the bus.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus that is signaling to return to the roadway after stopping. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Speed up to get away from them.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch your mirrors often. If another car is following too closely, slow down gradually and let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: When is it most important to be careful when turning or stopping in rain?

options.text: After it has rained all day.
A half hour after rain stops.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed off the road, creating a slippery mix with rainwater.

questions.question: A driver going much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let other cars pass.
May create danger for other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create danger for other drivers.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. On two-lane roads, if traffic backs up behind you, pull over and let cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when conditions require it.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?

options.text: One driver should go without stopping.
One driver should wave others ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver who arrived first.
questions.explanation: All four directions must stop at a four-way stop. The first vehicle to arrive should go first. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before finishing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This lets other drivers, riders, and pedestrians know your intentions.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A series of curves is ahead.
The road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road becomes slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is especially slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects safe driving the same way as:
questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol.
questions.explanation: Tiredness and alcohol have similar effects on driving ability. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours straight impairs driving about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.
